I implemented the `useFocusableInteractive` HTML accessibility lint rule.

**File created:** `crates/biome_html_analyze/src/lint/a11y/use_focusable_interactive.rs`

**Registration:** No manual edit to `mod.rs` was needed — the a11y group uses `declare_group_from_fs!`, which auto-discovers any `.rs` file in the directory. I verified the rule is discoverable via `RuleFilter::Rule("a11y", "useFocusableInteractive")` and the category `lint/a11y/useFocusableInteractive` was already present in `biome_diagnostics_categories`.

**How it works** (mirrors the existing JS rule, adapted to HTML):
- Queries `Aria<AnyHtmlTagElement>` (the opening tag node), so the diagnostic span (`node.syntax().text_trimmed_range()`) covers the element's opening tag.
- Uses `ctx.aria_roles().is_not_interactive_element(node)` to skip natively interactive elements (`<button>`, etc.).
- Requires a `role` attribute; checks it's interactive and non-composite via `AriaRole::from_roles(...).is_interactive() && !is_composite()` (so composite roles like `menu` are excluded).
- Only fires when there's no `tabindex` attribute (any value, including `0`/`-1`, suppresses it).

**Verified end-to-end** by running the analyzer through the real snapshot printer (`diagnostic_to_string`):

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `<div role="button">` | ✅ 1 diagnostic |
| `<div role="tab">` | ✅ 1 diagnostic |
| `<div role="button" tabindex="0">` | ✅ 0 |
| `<div role="button" tabindex="-1">` | ✅ 0 |
| `<button>` | ✅ 0 |
| `<div role="menu">` | ✅ 0 |
| `<h1 role="heading">` | ✅ 0 |

A key detail I caught: the quotes around `{role}` come from the attribute value node text (`to_trimmed_text()` includes the surrounding quotes), not from `<Emphasis>` — matching how the JS rule produces `"button"`. I used the quoted node text for display but the unquoted static value for the ARIA role lookup.
